chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked

about the game hunted in the unrestricted area (Al-Hill), then it is brought to the Sanctuary (Al-Haram) while it is alive. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he brings it into the Sanctuary, it becomes prohibited for him to eat it and to keep it. Therefore, do not buy in the Sanctuary except what has been slaughtered in the unrestricted area, then brought to the Sanctuary already slaughtered; there is no problem with the permissible (animals).'

key_terms.لِلْحَلَال: For the permissible (referring to the animal's status)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bringing live hunted game into the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific mechanism of prohibition, noting that the animal's status changes to 'haram' for consumption merely by entering the Haram boundaries while alive, a ruling derived from the sanctity of the space itself. The hadith provides a practical legal solution—slaughtering in the Hill before entry—which aligns with the Shia juristic principle that the act of slaughter must occur within permissible zones to maintain the meat's purity for the pilgrim. This ruling is particularly significant for understanding the distinction between the physical location of the kill versus the location of consumption in Hajj rituals.
